_comment: One agent's INSPECTION of every image extracted from the two Uganda sources attached to litlfred/smart-immunizations-uganda#1, produced by looking at each image (page-scan slides rendered from the PDF at 60 dpi). `draft` is applied as a DRAFT narrative that only a person may confirm (bun run cat narratives). Judgements a reviewer should check: slides 4, 7, 10 and 23 were filed `page-scan` by geometry; slides 7 (catch-up schedule) and 10 (target populations, service points) carry content that exists nowhere in the text layer, so they are re-filed as `figure` here, and slide 7's transcription is the ONLY source of the catch-up rules. The catch-up chart labels the 14-week IPV dose 'IPV1'; transcribed as printed.

Malaria, the fourteenth, is printed as slide text beside the graphic.

img-p006-1.saw: a vaccine-by-age grid with dose numbers in shaded cells and a colour legend
img-p006-1.draft: 'Current Immunization schedule': a grid with one row per vaccine and one column per age (Birth, 6 wks, 10 wks, 14 wks, 5 mo, 6 mo, 7 mo, 8 mo, 9 mo, 12 mo, 15 mo, 18 mo, 22 mo, 24 mo, 10 Yrs, 15-49 Yrs). Dose numbers by row: BCG 1 at birth; Hep B birth dose 1 at birth; Oral polio 0 at birth, 1 at 6 wks, 2 at 10 wks, 3 at 14 wks; DTP-HepB-Hib (penta) 1, 2, 3 at 6, 10, 14 wks; PCV 1, 2, 3 at 6, 10, 14 wks; Rotavirus 1, 2, 3 at 6, 10, 14 wks; Inactivated Polio 1 at 6 wks and 2 at 14 wks; Measles-Rubella 1 at 9 mo and 2 at 18 mo; Yellow Fever 1 at 9 mo; Malaria (row label in red) 1, 2, 3 at 6, 7, 8 mo and 4 at 18 mo; Vitamin A 1 at 6 mo, 2 at 12 mo, 3 at 18 mo, 4 at 24 mo; Deworming 1 at 12 mo; HPV 1 at 10 Yrs; Tetanus Diphtheria (TD) '1,2,3,4 &5' at 15-49 Yrs. The 5 mo, 15 mo and 22 mo columns are empty. Cell shading follows the slide's legend (slide text): dark grey 'previous on schedule'; light blue 'Newly introduced' (Hep B birth dose, IPV 1, Rotavirus 3, Measles-Rubella 2, Yellow Fever); orange 'Yet to be introduced' (Malaria 1 to 4, HPV).

img-p007-1.saw: a slide-sized chart: ages down the left, coloured vaccine bars, and 'When to give' / 'When not to give' columns; the slide has no text layer
img-p007-1.draft: 'Catch up schedule', headed "It is better to vaccinate late than never!". Rows by age: BIRTH (Hep B BD, BCG, OPV0), 6 WEEKS (OPV1, PCV1, DTP1, RV1, IPV1), 10 WEEKS (OPV2, PCV2, DTP2, RV2), 14 WEEKS (OPV3, PCV3, DTP3, RV3, a bar labelled IPV1), 9 MONTHS (MR1, YF), 18 MONTHS (MR2), 2 YEARS. Each vaccine's bar runs down the chart; stop-hand marks end Hep B BD at birth and rotavirus at 2 years. 'When to give': Hep B BD: As soon as possible after birth, ideally within 24 hours and up to 7 days; BCG: As soon as possible after birth; At 6 weeks (or as soon as possible thereafter); At 10 weeks (or as soon as possible thereafter), and at least 4 weeks after dose 1; At 14 weeks (or as soon as possible thereafter), and at least 4 weeks after dose 2; At 9 months (or as soon as possible thereafter); At 18 months (or as soon as possible there after), and at least 4 weeks since the previous dose. 'When not to give': Hep B BD: Not after 7 days; RV1: Not after 2 years of age; Not before 4 weeks has passed since the previous dose, RV2: Not after 2 years of age; Not before 4 weeks has passed since the previous dose, RV3: Not after 2 years of age; Not before 9 months of age (except where indicated)*; MR2: Not before 4 weeks has passed since MR1. Footnote: Even if a long time has passed between doses, there is no need to restart the series from the beginning. There is no upper age limit for most vaccines (except rotavirus < 2years and Hepatitis B BD <7 days).

img-p008-1.saw: a photograph of a seated baby with arrows from labels to body sites
img-p008-1.draft: 'Sites of child vaccines': a photograph of a seated baby with labelled arrows. Polio, Vitamin A, Rota (Oral) to the mouth; BCG (Intradermal) and Yellow Fever (Subcutaneous) to the baby's right upper arm; Measles-Rubella (Subcutaneous) to the baby's left upper arm; IPV (2cm apart) (Intramuscular) and PCV (2cm apart) (Intramuscular) to the baby's right thigh; Hep B Birth dose (Intramuscular) and DPT-HepB-Hib (Intramuscular) to the baby's left thigh. Sides are read from the arrows: the baby faces the viewer.
